A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REFINE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the relocated and renumbered learning curves.

before.justification: V1 reports original active-learning experiments on six image datasets, an ESC50 audio classification study, and filtering ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds biomedical and class-imbalance evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, and further comparative and diagnostic studies.

M1.justification: The main progressive-filtering algorithm and UHerding-based final selection remain unchanged. Appendix C adds tested second-stage variants that generate candidate batches with ensemble members and select among them using Fisher-information-ratio or expected-error criteria (Figure 11), constituting a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original image datasets and ESC50, while adding long-tailed Snacks and CIFAR-100 scenarios with imbalance ratios 10 and 50, plus BloodMNIST and DermaMNIST (Appendix D, Figure 12). These substantially expand class-distribution conditions and biomedical-domain coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds AutoAL to the ensemble comparisons, including Figure 4 and the complete learning curves. It also adds the label-privileged BoSS oracle to both individual and ensemble comparisons (Figures 14–17), expanding comparison scope to include an oracle reference alongside practical competitors.

E3.justification: The original main evaluation protocol is retained. Added protocols include batch sizes 10, 25, 50, and 100 under a fixed budget of approximately 2,500 labels, exponential class-imbalance construction with balanced-accuracy evaluation, and fine-tuning the last two DINOv2 transformer blocks with hyperparameters tuned on CIFAR-10 (Appendices C–D).

E4.justification: V2 adds controlled weak-member ensemble experiments, batch-size sensitivity, alternative second-stage selection, pool-shrinkage measurements, acquisition-time analysis, and robustness tests for imbalance, biomedical data, and partial fine-tuning. These substantially extend the original filtering-parameter and preprocessing-benefit ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 independent trials, but v1 explicitly omits standard errors whereas v2 displays them. Appendix E additionally reports a Friedman test across 18 dataset-by-model blocks followed by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction at significance level 0.01. No increase in existing trial counts is established.

E6.justification: Existing Figure 2 and Table 2 values and the reported 100% wins against SelectAL/TAILOR and 98% against TCM are retained. V2 adds a 97% win rate against AutoAL, BoSS reference curves, robustness and ablation outcomes, timings, and pool-retention measurements, including 0.052 for CIFAR-10 after five rounds. Table 3's parallel timings are projections rather than measured speedups.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2, Definition 1, Theorems 1–3, and Appendix A's proofs and numerical examples are unchanged. The added qualification about the practical validity of Theorem 3's assumption does not revise its formal assumptions or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims about progressive filtering, coverage-based REFINE, theoretical properties, and improved active-learning performance. Added experiments and comparisons provide further support without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendices C–E substantially expand interpretation of larger-batch benefits, weak-member ensembles, computational feasibility, applicability beyond frozen features, and the remaining gap to the BoSS oracle. Section 4.3 also newly acknowledges that the value-ordering assumption may fail in practice. The original dependence on ensemble quality remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the anonymous code placeholder and future-release statement with a concrete dal-toolbox repository URL. It also documents acquisition/training timings and parallel-runtime assumptions, including an 85% parallelizable fraction and scheduling overheads. These improve access and resource documentation without establishing changes to the original implementation settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations for AutoAL and BoSS, plus references supporting batch-ranking criteria, statistical tests, MedMNIST, and hyperparameter sensitivity. The central positioning against strategy-switching ensembles and single-step filtering remains intact; bibliographic metadata updates do not constitute additional scientific changes.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar, terminology, affiliation, and conclusion edits. It expands appendix subheadings, inserts an Additional Results and Experiments section, and moves the previous Appendix D learning-curve collection to Appendix E. The main narrative structure and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 redraws learning curves with uncertainty bands and oracle overlays, expands Figure 4 for AutoAL, and adds Figures 10–13 and Tables 3–4. The original complete learning-curve Figures 10–13 become Figures 14–17 with expanded legends and plotted comparisons, substantially revising the visual presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility and applicability. V1 omitted uncertainty displays and lacked targeted tests of imbalance, biomedical domain shift, and feature fine-tuning; v2 adds these checks, formal statistical comparisons, AutoAL and oracle references, and concrete code-access information. These address important evidential gaps while retaining the original results. Parallel speedups remain projections and some added-study settings are incompletely documented, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains.
